solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Set time for golfer’s play (4)

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it
T = time

annotation.surface: Someone books a tee time for a round of golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set time' reads as one idea, a booking, but splits into two pieces laid side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A putt is the gentle stroke a golfer plays on the green.

entries.clue: What transforms output from plant and energy for each factory (10)

blocks.note: pep = energy
per = for each, as in 'per head'
a mill is a factory

annotation.surface: An industrial question about what processes a power plant's output, with energy and factories in the frame.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' sounds industrial, like a power station, but it is a living plant, and its output is pepper. The mill grinds peppercorns into powder.
annotation.definitionFit: A peppermill turns peppercorns, the fruit of the pepper plant, into ground pepper.

entries.clue: Subject to irrational concerns to begin with (5)

indicatorNotes.to begin with: what comes to begin with is the first letter

blocks.note: used as it stands
pi is an irrational number
first letter of concerns

annotation.surface: Someone is prone to irrational worries from the outset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like a mood, but here it is maths: pi is the best-known irrational number.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the topic of a talk is its subject.

entries.clue: Standard complaint about one’s diet? (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the complaint goes about, around, the one

blocks.note: par is the standard, as in 'up to par'
a lament is a complaint
I = one, placed inside LAMENT

annotation.surface: A dieter grumbles about the usual food restrictions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diet' looks like food; it is also an old name for a national assembly, as in the Japanese Diet or the Diet of Worms.
annotation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly, which is what a parliament is.

entries.clue: Light racing rigs, which can appear on beaches? (9)

indicatorNotes.racing: letters that are racing are rushing about, out of order

blocks.note: amber is a traffic light
RIGS rearranged

annotation.surface: Lightweight racing boats or dune buggies turn up on the sand.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures light racing rigs on a beach; 'light' is really the amber of a traffic light, and the thing on the beach is washed-up whale secretion.
annotation.definitionFit: Ambergris, a waxy substance from sperm whales, is prized by perfumers and washes up on beaches.

entries.clue: Run away on the level (5)

blocks.note: British slang: to run off fast is to use your legs, two words closed up
slang short form of legitimate: honest, above board

annotation.surface: Someone bolts across flat ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is the two-word British slang 'leg it', run away fast, closed up into one word here.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are slang: to leg it is to run away, and something legit is honest, on the level.

entries.clue: Lover’s private message conveyed by broadcaster? (7)

indicatorNotes.conveyed by: what is conveyed by something is carried inside it

blocks.note: an airer is one who airs, broadcasts, something
DM = direct message, a private message on social media; it goes inside AIRER

annotation.surface: A lover's secret note is read out on air, as on a radio dedication show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests a radio station, but it is just AIRER, one who airs something.
annotation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor, someone romantically keen on another, which is a lover in the courting sense.

entries.clue: Stripped-down Tesco bid to get in India’s head chef (9)

indicatorNotes.Stripped-down: stripping a word removes its outer layer, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.to get in: the I is to get in, go inside, the bid

blocks.note: TESCO without its outer letters T and O
an offer is a bid
I = India in the NATO alphabet; it goes inside OFFER

annotation.surface: A supermarket makes a lean takeover bid to sign up a leading Indian chef.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain. The surface reads 'India's head chef' as one phrase, but India only supplies I and 'head chef' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Auguste Escoffier was the famous French head chef who ran the kitchens at the Savoy and Ritz hotels.

entries.clue: Fashion good for Chinese society (4)

blocks.note: the ton is fashion, high style, from French
G = good

annotation.surface: Good fashion sense matters in Chinese high society.
annotation.walkthrough: TON for fashion is dated English borrowed from French 'bon ton', and it turns up often in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society or association, especially one in an overseas Chinese community.

entries.clue: It can’t possibly sound (6)

indicatorNotes.possibly: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone insists that something simply cannot be right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but is the adjective meaning whole and undamaged.
annotation.definitionFit: Sound means undamaged, in good condition, and so does intact.

entries.clue: Decorator may want this very hot container of tea? (6,3)

blocks.note: piping hot means very hot
a tea bag holds the tea

annotation.surface: A painter and decorator asks for a mug of very hot tea.
annotation.walkthrough: The decorator is not a painter but a cake decorator, who pipes icing from a cone-shaped bag.
annotation.definitionFit: A piping bag is the cone of cloth or plastic a cake decorator squeezes icing through.

entries.clue: Crew welcoming company for wine (5)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: to welcome something is to take it in

blocks.note: to man a ship is to crew it
CO = company; it goes inside MAN

annotation.surface: A ship's crew greets its visitors with a glass of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crew' reads as a noun, a group of sailors, but it is the verb: to crew is to MAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine, red or white, from the Mâconnais district of Burgundy.

entries.clue: In plain language cake includes bun ultimately (2,5)

indicatorNotes.includes: the cake includes, holds, the letter

blocks.note: an éclair is a cream cake
last letter of bun; it goes inside ECLAIR after the E

annotation.surface: A baker describes, plainly, a cake with a bun baked into it.
annotation.walkthrough: EN CLAIR is a French phrase used in English for messages sent uncoded, in ordinary language rather than cipher.
annotation.definitionFit: En clair describes a message sent in plain language rather than in code.

entries.clue: Dispute imports are nearly qualifying for this? (6)

annotation.definition: Dispute imports are nearly qualifying for this?

indicatorNotes.imports: the dispute imports, takes in, the letters

blocks.note: a tiff is a quarrel
ARE without its last letter; it goes inside TIFF

annotation.surface: In a trade row, nearly all imports might be liable for a charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as the definition: in a trade dispute, imports are what a tariff is levied on. 'Imports' works twice, as the container instruction and as the goods.
annotation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax charged on imported goods, and tariffs are a common weapon in trade disputes.

entries.clue: Palace as erected under king in Seville that’s demolished (10)

indicatorNotes.erected under: in a down clue, AS built up above R sits on top of it
indicatorNotes.demolished: what is demolished is knocked apart, its letters scattered

blocks.note: used as it stands
R = king (rex); AS sits above it
joins AS and R as fodder

annotation.surface: A palace built in Seville under a king has since been pulled down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points to a Spanish palace such as the Alcázar, but Seville is only letters. AS and R combine with them before the whole lot is demolished.
annotation.definitionFit: Versailles is the vast palace outside Paris built for Louis XIV.

entries.clue: What’s compulsory for some padre’s offering? (8,7)

blocks.note: conscription: time in the armed forces some countries require
a padre is an army chaplain, and what he offers the troops is a church service

annotation.surface: Some worshippers must attend the chaplain's service.
annotation.walkthrough: A padre is a military chaplain, so the second sense is a religious service held for soldiers. The first is national service, required in some countries.
annotation.definitionFit: Military service is compulsory for conscripts, and a service conducted by an army padre is also a military service.

entries.clue: Stable worker’s irritable having cut pony’s hair (9)

indicatorNotes.having cut: the hair is cut, trimmed of its last letter

blocks.note: livery is an old word for irritable, like liverish
MANE, a pony's neck hair, with the last letter cut off

annotation.surface: A grumpy stable hand has been trimming a pony's mane.
annotation.walkthrough: A livery stable is one where horses are kept or hired out for a fee, and a liveryman works there.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by trade: livery stables keep and hire out horses, and the man employed there takes his title from them.

entries.clue: Stiffening wound round supporting structure (9)

indicatorNotes.round: the wound goes round the structure

blocks.note: a sting is a wound, as from a bee
an arch supports a bridge or roof; it goes inside STING

annotation.surface: A bandage wound round a brace stiffens it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as the past tense of wind, coiled round, but it is the noun, an injury.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by process: starch is the stiffener laundries apply to collars and shirts.

entries.clue: Something people always want to raise being flags? (6,9)

annotation.definition: Something people always want to raise

blocks.note: being, existing, is living
standards are flags

annotation.surface: Flags are always something people want to run up a pole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raise' fits flags neatly, which is the surface, but it also fits the definition: people want their living standards raised.
annotation.definitionFit: Living standards, the level of comfort people live in, are what every voter wants raised.

entries.clue: Not one of the pair I found in Underground? (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: the I is found in, inside, the other word

blocks.note: nether means lower, below ground, as in the nether world
used as it stands; it goes inside NETHER

annotation.surface: Someone discovers on the London Underground that neither of a pair is there.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital U makes 'Underground' look like the London Tube, but it is just NETHER, lower down.
annotation.definitionFit: Neither means not one and not the other of two.

entries.clue: Shapeless lump of a model getting little work (6)

blocks.note: a doll is a model of a person
OP = opus, a work, abbreviated

annotation.surface: A fashion model who barely works is dismissed as a shapeless lump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little work' is a standard way to ask for OP, the short form of opus.
annotation.definitionFit: A dollop is a soft shapeless lump, as of cream or mash.

entries.clue: Mind supporter at home games ignoring Lions? (6)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: games ignoring something leaves that part out

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
in = at home
GAMES without GAME; lions are big game

annotation.surface: A fan at a home fixture pays no attention to the Lions, the British and Irish rugby side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lions' looks like the rugby team, but lions are big game, so GAMES ignoring GAME leaves only S.
annotation.definitionFit: Brains means intelligence, a good mind.

entries.clue: Bundle of dynamite perhaps not quite secure outside? (5)

indicatorNotes.not quite: not quite drops the last letter
indicatorNotes.outside: the shortened word goes outside the explosive

blocks.note: SAFE without its last letter
HE = high explosive, of which dynamite is an example; it goes inside SAF

annotation.surface: A bundle of dynamite is not quite securely stowed outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bundle of dynamite' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Bundle'. 'Perhaps' shows dynamite is only an example of HE.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, of corn stalks or papers.

entries.clue: Charlie is unaccompanied going around Luxor sculptures (7)

indicatorNotes.going around: going around turns the letters to face the other way

blocks.note: C = Charlie in the NATO alphabet
used as it stands
solo = unaccompanied

annotation.surface: A man named Charlie tours the sculptures of Luxor on his own.
annotation.walkthrough: The Colossi of Memnon are two huge stone statues of a pharaoh near Luxor in Egypt.
annotation.definitionFit: Colossi, plural of colossus, are gigantic statues, and the Colossi of Memnon stand at Luxor.

entries.clue: Horse and what may be bet on it, mostly before end of race (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly keeps all but the last letter
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.clueFragment: what may be bet on it, mostly
blocks.note: SHIRT, as in 'bet your shirt on it', without its last letter
last letter of race

annotation.surface: A punter weighs up a horse and how much to stake on it before the race finishes.
annotation.walkthrough: To bet your shirt on something is to stake everything on it. 'It' in the surface is the horse, so the clue reads smoothly as racing talk.
annotation.definitionFit: A shire is a large, heavy British breed of draught horse.

entries.clue: British pass up League of Nations? (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, going up reverses the letters

blocks.note: B = British
a col is a mountain pass

annotation.surface: Britain gives up its seat in the League of Nations, the interwar body.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals point to the interwar League of Nations, but here it is any league of nations, a bloc.
annotation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations allied for a common purpose, a league of nations in the lower-case sense.

entries.clue: Clear fluid left larva without nitrogen (5)

blocks.note: L = left
NYMPH, an insect larva, without N, the symbol for nitrogen

annotation.surface: A lab notes a clear fluid left behind by a larva lacking nitrogen.
annotation.walkthrough: A nymph is the young stage of insects like dragonflies, so it stands in for larva here.
annotation.definitionFit: Lymph is the colourless fluid that circulates through the body's lymphatic system.

entries.clue: Adroit lie ruined newspaper piece (9)

indicatorNotes.ruined: what is ruined is wrecked, its letters thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A clever falsehood has spoiled a newspaper article.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a press scandal: a skilful lie wrecks an article, and the article is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An editorial is the article setting out a newspaper's own opinion.

entries.clue: Church refuting circulating scientific article based on spin (10)

indicatorNotes.circulating: circulating letters move around into a new order

blocks.note: CE = Church of England
REFUTING rearranged

annotation.surface: The Church circulates a rebuttal of a scientific paper that is mere spin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scientific article' reads as a paper and 'spin' as PR, but the article is an object, and the spin is literal rotation.
annotation.definitionFit: A centrifuge is laboratory apparatus that separates substances by spinning them fast.

entries.clue: Less intelligent individuals wanting lecturer’s explanatory lists (4)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so the lecturer is removed

blocks.note: DONKEYS, fools, without DON, a university lecturer

annotation.surface: The duller students need their lecturer's handouts explained.
annotation.walkthrough: A donkey is a dimwit, and a don is a university lecturer.
annotation.definitionFit: A key is the explanatory list on a map or chart saying what its symbols mean.
